---
title: "Lesson 5: Previewing and rendering"
---

## Preview vs. render

| | **Preview** | **Render** |
|---|---|---|
| What it does | Builds the site and opens it in a browser or panel. **Updates automatically** every time you save | Builds the whole site into the output folder (`docs/`) once |
| Use it | While you're writing | Before you commit and publish |
| Command | `quarto preview` | `quarto render` |

::: {.callout-important title="Stop the preview before rendering"}
Running preview and render at the same time can cause errors. Stop the preview first (**Ctrl + C** in its terminal, or close the preview panel).
:::

## Previewing

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## Positron

- Open any `.qmd` file and press **Cmd + Shift + K** (Mac) / **Ctrl + Shift + K** (Windows), or click the **Preview** button above the file.
- The site opens in the **Viewer** pane. Save a file and it refreshes.
- To open it in your web browser, click the **Open in browser** icon in the Viewer.

## VS Code

- Open any `.qmd` file and press **Cmd + Shift + K** (Mac) / **Ctrl + Shift + K** (Windows), or click the **Preview** button above the file.
- The site opens in a side panel. Save a file and it refreshes.

## RStudio

- Open any `.qmd` file and click **Render** (or press **Cmd + Shift + K** / **Ctrl + Shift + K**).
- Check **Render on Save** next to the Render button to refresh on every save.
- The page opens in the **Viewer** pane, or in a browser, depending on the gear menu next to Render.

## Terminal

From the project folder:

```bash
quarto preview
```

It prints a local address (like `http://localhost:4321`) and opens your browser. Leave it running while you edit; press **Ctrl + C** to stop.

:::

The preview is only on your computer. Nobody else can see it.

## Rendering the whole site

::: {.panel-tabset group="editor"}

## Positron

Open a terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**) and run:

```bash
quarto render
```

## VS Code

Open a terminal (**Terminal → New Terminal**) and run:

```bash
quarto render
```

## RStudio

Go to the **Build** tab and click **Render Website**. Or, in the **Terminal** tab (not the R Console):

```bash
quarto render
```

## Terminal

From the project folder:

```bash
quarto render
```

:::

Quarto lists each page as it builds:

```
[1/4] index.qmd
[2/4] about.qmd
[3/4] data-sources.qmd
[4/4] lessons/01-intro.qmd

Output created: docs/index.html
```

Open `docs/index.html` in a browser to check the result.

## Pages with R code: freeze

When you render, Quarto runs the R code on every page. That can be slow, and anyone who renders the site needs every R package used.

**Freeze** saves the results, so code only re-runs when that page's code changes:

```yaml
# in _quarto.yml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

Quarto stores the saved results in a `_freeze/` folder. **Commit `_freeze/`** along with `docs/`.

If a page's code needs passwords, internal servers, or real data, it shouldn't run on a website at all. Use `eval: false` to show it without running it, and never publish its output.

## Common errors and fixes

| Error message contains… | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `YAML parse error` / `bad indentation` | A spacing mistake in `_quarto.yml` or a page header | Check indentation (two spaces per level, no tabs) and the space after each colon |
| `property name ... is invalid` | A setting in the wrong place (e.g., `logo:` under `website:` instead of `navbar:`) | Check the [Quarto reference](https://quarto.org/docs/reference/projects/websites.html) for where the setting goes |
| `there is no package called 'ggplot2'` | An R package isn't installed | `install.packages("ggplot2")` |
| `R installation not found` / `knitr` not found | Quarto can't find R, or knitr isn't installed | Run `quarto check`; install `rmarkdown` and `knitr`; restart the editor |
| `Error in ... : object 'x' not found` (with a chunk name) | The R code has an error | Run that chunk in R to debug. The message tells you which chunk failed |
| `Unable to resolve link target` (warning) | A link points to a file that doesn't exist | Fix the path or file name |
| A page is missing from the site | It's not in the navbar/sidebar, or not in a `render:` list | Add it to `_quarto.yml` |

::: {.callout-tip}
Read the **first** error message. Later messages are often just consequences of the first one.
:::
